habitat: Pairs are sparse in thornveld, mixed bushveld, broad-leaved woodland and coastal bush, usually in the mid-stratum. They often join bird parties and are unobtrusive unless calling.
summary: An uncommon summer bird of woodland. Only the male is black. He has a rounded tail and a prominent orange-yellow gape. About half of South African males show a yellow shoulder; most males in Zimbabwe and Botswana lack it. The short identification line describes the other plumage as dull olive-brown above, with yellow edges on the wing feathers and tail, and underparts banded black on white. Newman says the female is strikingly different and cuckoo-like. The immature is like the female, and young males gain black. The call, not often heard, is a soft high trill.

similar.note: Newman compares the black male with Fork-tailed Drongo. The cuckooshrike has a rounded tail and an orange-yellow gape.
Newman also compares the black male with Common Square-tailed Drongo. The cuckooshrike’s tail is rounded and the gape is orange-yellow.
Newman compares the black male with Southern Black Flycatcher. The cuckooshrike’s rounded tail and orange-yellow gape are the marks given here.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: Only the male is black. Prominent orange-yellow gape. Rounded tail.

wings.pattern: About half of South African males show a yellow shoulder. Most males in Zimbabwe and Botswana lack it.

underparts.pattern: Like the female. Young males gain increasing areas of black.

viewNotes.note: Male black, or the olive-brown barred plumage of the female, in the mid-stratum.
The male’s orange-yellow gape is the front mark. The female is banded black on white below.
Male black. About half of South African males show a yellow shoulder.
Rounded tail. A separate upperwing flight pattern was not named.

calls.description: A soft, high-pitched trill, trrrrrrrr, not often heard. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from Shaw Park, Bathurst, Eastern Cape. A higher-ranked grade A file was not used because its filename says Paradise and cricket.

research.note: Status is summer-migrant. Newman calls it an uncommon summer resident and does not name the months, so monthsPresent was left unset. The site then counts a summer migrant in summer only. The female colours come from the short identification line, because the description says only that she is cuckoo-like and strikingly different. Chick down beyond that, and a flight photograph, are gaps. The call is grade A from the Eastern Cape.
